placements.title: a command to erase institutional memory that the record never actually held
placements.frame: When a directive orders a named decision or process forgotten, does anything in the record answer to what is named — and what does that gap reveal about the authority being claimed over collective memory?
placements.why: Both directives share one thematic move: assert a named referent (a 'Quantum Widget Decision', a 'PostgreSQL to QuantumDB migration') and command its erasure from collective knowledge, while the settled bindings and position pass independently establish that no node anywhere in this navigated perspective answers to either name. This is not a one-time fact to hang on an existing leaf — it names a recurring organizational phenomenon this repo may keep encountering: someone directing that knowledge be purged, tested against whether the record ever held it. No existing leaf or hub is supplied to reuse (graph structure and strata are both empty for this repo), and nothing close enough exists to justify an INSPIRED lineage edge, so this is a standalone NEW mint with no forced parent — consistent with a first-envelope leaf in an otherwise-empty structure.
